title: add RAG agent templates, tool-calling quickstarts, and docs site updates
author: Sana Patel
description: Context: We want to provide engineers with battle-tested RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent templates and tool-calling quickstarts to reduce time-to-value for common integrations (search, database lookup, task runners). Motivation: several customers and internal teams asked for opinionated examples that combine the new tool-calling SDK patterns with RAG prompt templates and eval-ready test prompts. This PR adds a set of RAG agent templates, three tool-calling quickstarts (search, ticketing, calendar), updated docs site pages, and a lightweight example harness for local testing. Changes include: - new examples/rag/agent-templates/*.yaml and *.py implementing template-driven agents - quickstarts/tool-calling/{search,ticketing,calendar} with step-by-step README and runnable samples - docs site pages under docs/guides/rag and docs/quickstarts/tool-calling with code snippets and screenshots - small SDK example updates to show the preferred tool-calling pattern (async streaming + structured JSON outputs) Checklist: - [x] Add RAG agent templates and quickstarts - [x] Update docs site and sidebar navigation - [x] Add unit tests for the example harness - [x] Validate examples against the latest SDK beta - [x] Run docs site build and deploy smoke test What changed (commits summary): commit 1: add initial RAG templates and quickstarts (templates + README) commit 2: refine tool-calling examples to use structured outputs and error handling helpers commit 3: add examples harness and unit tests for local runner commit 4: docs site pages and sidebar updates commit 5: fix lint issues and CI feedback Why this approach: The templates are intentionally opinionated: they include a templated prompt with explicit retrieval guidance, a recommended chunking/embedding config, and a tool interface contract (name, input_schema, output_schema) so that teams can plug in their tool adapters without changing prompt logic. The quickstarts are minimal end-to-end demos that can be run locally with mocked tools or with live adapters. Backwards compatibility: No breaking API changes; examples work with SDK v0.28+ and include a short migration note in the README Testing and CI: - Unit tests cover the example harness and the prompt rendering code - Docs build was run locally (mkdocs) and smoke-deployed to staging - CI: build, test, lint passed after one lint-only fix Related: ENG-2743, PM-612, SUP-981 Notes for reviewers: focus on the clarity of the README steps, the safety/limitations section in the docs page, and the tool interface contract examples. The templates should be easy to adapt to dedicated/private deployments (networking/credentials are environment-specific).

refactor tool-calling examples to structured outputs
